subject: Re: Mutual action playbook & benchmark — AuroraData performance MAP
messages:
From: James Bishop <james.bishop@auroradata.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@auroradata.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — MAP + perf targets for long-context evaluation

Tessa —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Aurora is keen to move to a short MAP so we can validate Redwood’s inference characteristics against a production prompt mix. High level asks:

- We need a MAP that shows end-to-end latency (P50/P90/P99), throughput at target concurrency, and TTFT (time-to-first-token) across our top-3 prompt classes.
- Long-context validation: we want tests that stress max sequence length to 128k tokens (where supported), and intermediate buckets: 8k, 32k, 64k.
- KV-cache behavior: measure incremental generation when continuing conversations using cached prefixes vs cold starts.

Can your team propose a short evaluation plan and an estimate for how long the MAP should take? Our procurement team also needs a perf report to sign off on committed capacity.

Appreciate a sketch and timeline — attaching our sanitized sample prompt set.

Regards,
James
Director, Data Products — AuroraData

Attachment: aurora_prompt_set_sample_20270609.json (sanitized prompt examples)
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: James Bishop <james.bishop@auroradata.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — MAP + perf targets for long-context evaluation

James —

Thanks for the sample prompts and for the time yesterday. Attached is a short MAP playbook and an evaluation plan draft. TL;DR: we can run a focused MAP in ~5 business days if Aurora provides the final prompt distribution and a handful of representative conversations for KV-cache runs.

High-level MAP milestones (proposed):
1) Alignment call & data handoff (1 business day)
2) Test harness setup & baseline runs (1 day)
3) Long-context / max-seq sweeps + KV-cache scenarios (2 days)
4) Analysis & review deliverable (1 day)

Primary metrics we’ll capture:
- Latency: P50/P90/P99 per prompt-class and sequence-length bucket
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec at 1, 4, 8, 16 concurrent streams (configurable)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) distribution by model variant and VCPU/GPU type
- KV-cache delta: cold-start vs cached prefixes (time & token-cost delta)
- Memory / GPU utilization & quantization effects (32-bit vs int8/4-bit where applicable)

We’ll use a synthetic traffic replay of your prompt distribution and then a small subset of live-conversation continuations to exercise KV-cache. Karthik will define the harness and specific flags (e.g., max_chunk_size, cache_prune) in the test plan.

Next step: quick alignment call this afternoon or tomorrow? If procurement needs a perf artifact for commit, we’ll mark the MAP_Benchmark_Report as a deliverable in the MAP and include raw metrics CSVs.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Playbook_AuroraData_v1.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: James Bishop <james.bishop@auroradata.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — MAP + perf targets for long-context evaluation

James / Tessa —

A few technical clarifications to make the benchmarking deterministic:

1) Sequence-length buckets: we will run four buckets: 256-2048 (short), 2049-8192 (mid), 8193-32768 (long), and 32769-131072 (max). For each bucket, we sample 200 prompts from your distribution.

2) KV-cache scenarios:
   - Cold-start: single-shot generation with no cache warmup.
   - Warmed-prefix: load first N tokens (N configurable; default 4096) then continue generation. Measure incremental latency and token cost for continuation vs cold-start.

3) Concurrency sweep: run at concurrency levels {1, 4, 8, 16}. For each concurrency point we will run 3 repeats and aggregate P50/P90/P99.

4) TTFT measurement: capture both server-side TTFT and end-to-end client perceived TTFT (includes network/SDK overhead). We will surface both.

5) Run env: We’ll execute on a dedicated Redwood cluster with pinned model variant (quantized int8 and baseline fp16) and expose kernel selection logs so you can audit perf deltas.

I’ll check in once the harness is wired and we have an initial baseline.

—Karthik
Senior Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: James Bishop <james.bishop@auroradata.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@auroradata.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — MAP + perf targets for long-context evaluation

Tessa / Karthik —

Thanks for the clear plan. We authorized the handoff yesterday — attaching the full prompt distribution and 25 representative conversation traces for KV-cache tests. Please run the baseline and the long-window sweep. Procurement wants an initial numbers artifact (CSV + short summary) by EOD Wednesday.

Note on acceptance criteria: for committed capacity we need either P90 latency <= 220ms on short prompts at 8 concurrency, or a documented fallback plan with cost/latency tradeoffs. Also want TTFT <= 40ms median for the short prompt class; if kernel selection or quantization increases TTFT we need to see the delta.

Best,
James

Attachments: aurora_prompt_distribution_20270613.json, aurora_convo_traces_25.zip
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: James Bishop <james.bishop@auroradata.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action playbook — benchmark deliverables (summary)

James —

Attached is the MAP_Benchmark_Report_v1.pdf and the raw metrics CSVs (Aurora_raw_metrics_20270614.csv). Summary highlights below:

- Baseline (fp16) short-prompt (256–2k) at concurrency=8: P50=32ms, P90=210ms, P99=355ms. Meets Aurora acceptance for P90 but P99 shows tail risk at sustained bursts.
- TTFT (client-perceived median) short-prompt: 37ms. TTFT delta between fp16 and int8 quant: +5ms median for int8 (kernel warmup and smaller compute batches).
- Throughput: at concurrency=8, we sustained 1.8k requests/min on fp16 baseline for short prompts; tokens/sec varied by sequence length bucket as expected.
- Long-context behavior: for 32k and 64k buckets the P90 increased ~3–5x relative to short prompts; for max (>=32k) we recommend batching policies and KV-prefix pruning to reduce GPU memory pressure.
- KV-cache: warmed-prefix continuations showed a 45–60% reduction in CPU & GPU token cost for continuation vs cold-start, and incremental latency (continuation-only) reduced by ~60% for average continuation lengths of 512 tokens.

Action items / next steps:
- Marissa will coordinate a technical debrief next Tue to walk through kernel selection logs and quantization tradeoffs.
- We’ll add a canary rollout plan into the MAP to trigger fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if P99 crosses 400ms for >5% traffic.
- Deliverables: MAP_Benchmark_Report_v1.pdf (attached), raw metrics CSV (attached), and a short runbook for KV-cache configuration tweaks.

If this is acceptable, I’ll update the MAP milestones and share a final schedule for Dedicated capacity onboarding.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Benchmark_Report_v1.pdf, Aurora_raw_metrics_20270614.csv
